info.title: Time
info.description: Time ensures that workers' time is recorded, workers are paid, and that overall project costs are tracked.

tags.name: Time_Timesheets
tags.description:
Timesheets ensure that workers are paid appropriately. They also help project managers invoice clients and track overall project costs and expenses over time. Timesheets are used in both Projects and Time & Expenses. 

Each time a timesheet entry is submitted, a timesheet approval history object is created for tracking purposes. Many settings that impact required timesheet information are configured in Projects. For more information, see [Configure Projects](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Setting_Up_the_Projects_Application) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Time_Timesheet lines
tags.description:
A timesheet line is an entry on a timesheet that represents work done by one employee on a single day. Each timesheet line should reflect the dimensions used by the company. That is, work done for one customer or project should be recorded in a separate timesheet line from work done for another customer or project, etc. Reports and invoices use the dimension values to group timesheet lines for billing.

For more information, see [Fill out timesheets](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Fill_out_timesheets) in the Sage Intacct Help center.

tags.name: Time_Time types
tags.description: Time types capture and track categories of time, such as salary, contract hours, overtime, vacation, and travel time. When you use time types, you can generate improved reports that use time types to identify project work time for your categories. You can also use time types to post labor costs to general ledger accounts. For more information, see [Add time types](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Add_time_types).

tags.name: Time_Approve timesheet
tags.description:
The approval and decline processes are generally the same. You can approve or decline an entire timesheet or only portions of it (individual days).

A partially approved or declined timesheet includes a mix of approved or declined and submitted time entries. The last action determines whether the timesheet status appears as partially approved or declined. For example, if you last approved entries, the timesheet appears as partially approved; if you last declined entries, the timesheet appears as partially declined.

tags.name: Time_Timesheet approval records
tags.description:
An approval record is the history of a specific timesheet entry’s approvals. An approval record does not exist for timesheet entries that are auto-approved or those that do not require approval. Approvals can include from 1 to 5 levels. For example, a level 1 approval might simply require a department manager's approval. A level 2 approval might require a department manager's approval followed by a department director's approval.

 The approval record also includes the current approval state. Approval states are: Submitted, Pending Approval, Approved, and Declined. For more information about timesheet approval status, see [Track timesheet status](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Track_timesheet_status).

tags.name: Time_Timesheet rules
tags.description: Set up timesheet rules to enforce policies when an employee enters a timesheet. Timesheets that don't meet the rules cannot be submitted. Create a timesheet rule that's global to apply across an entire organization. Or, create a timesheet rule that applies only to a specific holiday schedule or designated project workers. Create specific timesheet rules if projects span multiple departments or multiple entities that have different work schedules. See [Specify timesheet rules](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_Viewing_Timesheet_Rules) in the Sage Intacct Help Center for more information.

objects.time.timesheet.description: Header information for timesheets. Includes employee name, period begin date, period end date, GL post date, description, and attachments.

key.description: System-assigned unique key for the timesheet.

id.description: Unique identifier for the timesheet. This value is same as the key for this object.

beginDate.description: Begin date of the work period.

endDate.description: The calculated end date of the work period, based on the `beginDate`.

postingDate.description: Defaults to timesheet `endDate`. If `endDate` falls within a closed GL period, then `postingDate` automatically defaults to the first day of the next open GL period.

state.description: State of the timesheet in the approval cycle, such as approved or declined.

unitOfMeasure.description: Unit of measure, such as hours or days, used in labor cost calculations. Maps to configuration set in Projects and cannot be changed.

hoursInDay.description: Hours in a day. Used to calculate labor cost.

description.example: Week of 2024-01-01 to cover help desk

calculationMethod.description: The calculation method used for pay and defined by `time-type.earningType`. Used in labor cost and billing calculations. When `null`, the labor amount does not calculate for the timesheet. For example, labor costs for certain roles, such as management or sales, might not need to be calculated.

postActualLaborCost.description: Only `true` when `employee.postActualCostWithVariance` is set to `true` to indicate that `calculationMethod` is `salary`. When `employee.postActualCostWithVariance` is set to false, `calculationMethod` is `hourly`, so `postActualLaborCost` is `false`.

employee.description: The employee who performed the work and whose time is being tracked.

firstName.description: The first name of the contact.

lastName.description: The last name of the contact.
